reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes wear-resistant microstructures in different alloys and a Y2O3-reinforced composite, but neither provides any support for stress-assisted impurity segregation, brittle precipitate nucleation, or a ductile-to-brittle transition in a single-phase HEA under the proposed conditions.
premises: Stress-assisted impurity mobility and segregation occur in single-phase HEAs under demanding loading
Segregation leads to nucleation of brittle intermetallic precipitates along grain boundaries
These precipitates cause a transition from ductile to brittle fracture and loss of toughness
The mechanism is active at elevated temperatures and/or high strain rates
